feature: Money path — refund (charge.refunded) is LOG-ONLY. This manifest pins the real, current behavior: a refund event changes NO subscription/billing DB state anywhere in the platform. It exists to document the gap honestly and to flag the day that behavior changes.
notes: Epic #803 (Money-path lifecycle coverage). Drives the REAL msp-billing-webhook handleChargeRefundedZohoNote via the dev-origin-gated POST /api/admin/testbed/billing-simulate (same dispatchMspStripeEvent as production). Honest boundary + self-contained testbed setup: see payment-failed-dunning.json notes.

*** GAP BEING DOCUMENTED ***: charge.refunded is the ONLY refund handling in the entire repo, and it is a LOG-ONLY warning (artifacts/api-server/src/routes/msp-billing-webhook.ts handleChargeRefundedZohoNote). It writes nothing to msp_subscriptions, msp_event_store, invoices, or anywhere else, and does not distinguish a full from a partial refund. There is no refund state machine on any channel (MSP or direct-customer). So a refund today leaves the platform's own records completely unchanged — the accounting correction is expected to happen manually in Zoho Books.

This manifest therefore asserts the CURRENT correct behavior: after a charge.refunded event the testbed subscription is UNCHANGED (still active) and NO event row was written. It is intentionally a change-detector: if/when real refund handling is implemented (e.g. a 'refunded' state or a credit-note event), this manifest MUST be updated to assert the new state — a failure here after such a change is the signal, not a bug in the test.
